task_statement:
Research question (as posed on 2026-11-01, in the area of player absence and offensive reorganization):
The teammate with the closest pre-absence initiation profile (or most minutes / initiations / same-position minutes) is the largest gainer in the absent player's primary types.

Data available on that date:
- NBA 2022-23 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2023-24 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2024-25 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2025-26 regular season (complete from 2026-04-13; partial before)
- NBA 2025-26 playoffs (complete from 2026-06-21; partial before)
- Sources: Per-game files from the NBA stats API: play-by-play (action type, sub-type, clock, period, score, player, shot distance and result), substitution rotation intervals, starters, defensive matchup minutes and partial possessions, box-score summary. Derived play-type possession records (initiator, play type, points) in a graph database built from the play-by-play.
- Units available to a study of this question (as recorded): n=148; 148 spells; 11 cases

Your job is to decide, before any analysis is run, whether this question can be answered with this data, what has already been established about it, which methodological and statistical risks threaten a test of it, and either a pre-registration-quality design or a reasoned recommendation not to proceed.

own_inferences: The question is framed to compare performance of a specific teammate relative to others after a teammate’s absence, but the data set contains only 11 absence spells, which is likely insufficient for a robust statistical test of the proposed relationship. The absence of prior studies in the retrieval step suggests no established findings to build upon. The design of the study would require careful definition of “primary types” and a clear metric for “gainer,” both of which are not specified in the data description, adding additional uncertainty.
uncertainties: Exact definition of primary types and gainer metric; potential unmeasured confounders such as coaching changes or opponent strength; limited sample size may prevent achieving adequate power.

historical_effect.explanation: No historical evidence was retrieved; decision is based solely on data and methodological considerations.

blocking_constraints.text: Only 11 absence spells provide limited statistical power to detect effects in a potentially noisy environment.
Absence events are rare and clustered, reducing the effective sample size for comparative analysis.
Other team changes (lineup adjustments, injuries, coaching changes) may confound the relationship between teammate similarity and performance gains.

prior_work.summary: No prior work was retrieved that directly addresses this specific hypothesis.

risks.text: Insufficient number of absence spells to detect moderate effects at conventional significance levels.
Sparse exposure limits the ability to estimate treatment effects reliably.
Potential confounding by unmeasured variables that co-vary with absence events.
Unclear if the metrics for “primary types” and “gainer” are consistently measured across seasons.

design.estimand: Difference in performance gains attributable to the teammate with the closest pre-absence initiation profile relative to other teammates
design.unit: Teammate within a team after a teammate’s absence
design.sample: All 148 spells (11 absence cases) across five seasons
design.power: Insufficient power; minimum viable sample size not met
design.controls: None specified (due to limited data); would recommend controlling for team, opponent, and time in season if proceeding
design.falsification: Compare gains to teammates with the farthest initiation profiles as a negative control
design.decision_rule: Reject proceeding due to lack of sufficient data and methodological uncertainty
